newsitem.title: GERMANY: Agents say Lufthansa to cap commissions.
newsitem.headline: Agents say Lufthansa to cap commissions.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG is preparing to cap travel agents' commissions as part of its cost-saving plans, German travel agents said on Thursday at an industry meeting.
"It is clear that Lufthansa is preparing to cap commissions," said Achim Terrahe, marketing manager for Germany at travel agent group Carlson Wagonlit Travel.
Another agent, who asked not to be named, told Reuters: "Lufthansa is preparing the ground to announce commission cuts after a travel agent conference in November."
Lufthansa marketing executive Hemjoe Klein did not mention the issue during a speech to the meeting, but the airline in the past has denied it had plans to cap commissions.

The comments by travel industry officials followed a presentation by Roland Berger, chairman of Roland Berger & Partner GmbH, in which he outlined how automobile manufacturers had reduced standard commission payments but introduced performance bonuses.
His group has been advising Lufthansa on the savings potential of such programmes.

Berger told the conference that they had three basic future options in the travel world -- mass-market growth by joining large agency groups, specialisation on high-value niche products or selling out of the business.
